title: Point evaluation on perfect models respects derived completion
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $P$ be a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules (a perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]), let $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R)$, and set $C=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline P$ and $J=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{P^\vee}$ using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-hom-complex].
Then the canonical map $J\to R\mathcal Hom_B(C,B)$ is an isomorphism, and $J$, $C$, and $C\otimes_B^LJ$ belong to the derived-complete bounded constructible integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $\chi_Q:Q\to R\varprojlim_m(Q\otimes_B^L(R/\varpi^m)_s)$ for the specified strict-cone completion map [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] at the identity extension, and $\widehat{\operatorname{ev}}:C\widehat\otimes_R^LJ\to B$ for the completed evaluation of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $q_P:\Gamma(s,J)\to P^\vee$ be the comparison $h\mapsto(x\mapsto h(1\otimes x))$ of [lem-pod-point-derived-hom-evaluation] on these perfect models. Under the canonical unit $P\cong\Gamma(s,C)$ and point tensor comparison $\tau:\Gamma(s,C\widehat\otimes_R^LJ)\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_R^L\Gamma(s,J)$ of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], one has
$$\Gamma(s,\widehat{\operatorname{ev}})=\operatorname{ev}_{P,R}\circ(1_P\otimes q_P)\circ\tau.$$
This uses the specified completion comparisons $\chi_Q$, including their quotient-map product component and zero shifted-product component, and is equality of derived morphisms.

source.place: Second sentence at integral coefficients: finite-projective Hom models and compatibility of evaluation with the strict-cone completeness comparison

proof.text: Put $L(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$. The valuation-ring lemma makes $R$ a PID, hence Noetherian by the PID lemma. Constant sheafification is exact by the constant-module section lemma, and $B$ is flat over $\underline R$ by the completed-constant reduction lemma. Consequently $L$ is exact. Sections $\Gamma(s,-)$ on $B$-modules are exact by the point-sections theorem. The sheaf-tensor universal property gives the adjunction $L\dashv\Gamma(s,-)$: $h$ corresponds to $x\mapsto h_s(1\otimes x)$; the inverse sends $t$ to $b\otimes x\mapsto b\,t(x)|_U$. These formulas respect balancing and restrictions and are inverse on the generators $1\otimes x$.

source.place: Tags 093J, 093M (lemma-constant-exact, lemma-completion-flat); extension/sections adjunction on generators

proof.text: The scheme $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is nonempty, connected, separated and of finite type over $k$. Clause (1) of connected-constant $H^0$ therefore identifies $\Gamma(s,(R/\varpi^m)_s)=R/\varpi^m$ through the constant-value map, for every $m\geq1$. Limits of sheaves are computed sectionwise, so $\Gamma(s,B)=\varprojlim_mR/\varpi^m=R$; the last equality is the ring isomorphism given by the quotient maps in the integers-profinite-tower lemma. Thus all three extra hypotheses (exact $L$, exact $\Gamma$, and this constant-value identification) of point-sections reconstruction and point-derived-Hom evaluation hold. The adjunction is exactly their displayed adjunction, not an abstractly chosen one.

source.place: Second sentence, point coefficients: verification of the actual sections/extension comparison

proof.text: Each $P^i$ is a summand of a finite free module. Applying duals and tensor products to its splitting shows that $(P^i)^\vee$ and $P^i\otimes_R(P^j)^\vee$ are finite projective. Hence $P$, $P^\vee$, and $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RP^\vee)$ are bounded finite-projective complexes; their cohomology is finitely generated because $R$ is Noetherian. Point-sections reconstruction therefore gives $L(P),L(P^\vee),L(T)\in D^b_c(s,R)$, including derived completeness and a uniform bound for all reductions. The termwise balancing isomorphism $(b\otimes x)\otimes(b'\otimes f)\mapsto bb'\otimes(x\otimes f)$ identifies $C\otimes_B J$ with $L(T)$. Each term of $C$ and $J$ is a summand of a finite sum of $B$, hence flat, so the bounded-above-flat K-flat lemma says their total tensor computes $C\otimes_B^LJ$. This proves all three membership assertions. The same reconstruction applied to $R[0]$ gives $B\in D^b_c(s,R)$. Its unit and that for $P$ are the actual maps $r\mapsto r$ and $x\mapsto1\otimes x$.

source.place: Second sentence, perfect point models: dual and tensor models and their derived-complete constructibility

proof.text: Apply the bounded-summand-of-finite-free internal-Hom model with first complex $C$ and second complex $B[0]$. Its boundedness hypotheses hold because $P$ is bounded. It identifies $R\mathcal Hom_B(C,B)$ with $\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(C,B)$. The natural map $B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^i,R)}\to\mathcal Hom_B(L(P^i),B)$ sends $b\otimes f$ to $(b'\otimes x\mapsto bb'f(x))$. For $P^i=R^r$ this is the identity on $B^r$; applying the inclusion and projection of a finite-free splitting makes it an isomorphism for $P^i$. These identifications commute with precomposition by $d_P$ and with multiplication, so, using $d(f)=d_Bf-(-1)^{\deg f}fd_C$, they form an isomorphism of Hom complexes $J\cong\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(C,B)$. It is the canonical arrow specified by evaluation. Thus $J\to R\mathcal Hom_B(C,B)$ is the claimed isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08JI, lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free; finite-summand calculation of its terms

proof.text: Let $D=C\otimes_B J$ denote the ordinary tensor model from step 3, and write $e:D\to B$ for ordinary derived evaluation using step 4. Apply point-derived-Hom evaluation with $c=P$; its K-flat requirement holds by step 3, and all its exactness and coefficient hypotheses were checked in steps 1–2. Comparing its K-injective model to the Hom model in step 4 gives exactly $q_P$, since both send $h$ to $x\mapsto h_s(1\otimes x)$. Let $\beta:P\otimes_R\Gamma(s,J)\to\Gamma(s,D)$ be the sections balancing map using the unit of $P$. The cited evaluation clause gives $\Gamma(s,e)\beta=\operatorname{ev}_{P,R}(1\otimes q_P)$. Explicitly, for $x\in P^p$ and $h$ of degree $j$, both sides take $x\otimes h$ to $(-1)^{pj}h_s(1\otimes x)$. This also fixes the order of the two tensor factors and the sign.

source.place: Second sentence, ordinary derived Hom/evaluation before completion

proof.text: Put $A_m=(R/\varpi^m)_s$. Because $C,J$ are bounded flat models, there is a termwise tower isomorphism $D\otimes_B A_m\cong(C\otimes_B A_m)\otimes_{A_m}(J\otimes_B A_m)$, sending $(c\otimes j)\otimes a$ to $(c\otimes1)\otimes(j\otimes a)$. It commutes with quotient transitions. Thus its strict-cone derived limit is exactly $C\widehat\otimes_R^LJ$ as defined by the integral operations. The identity-extension finite-free-completed comparison supplies isomorphisms $\chi_D:D\to C\widehat\otimes_R^LJ$ and $\chi_B:B\to R\varprojlim_m A_m$, since both objects are complete by step 3. In these models each is the map with product component the family of quotient maps and shifted-product component zero.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12(4), Proposition 3.5.1; specified strict-cone normalization from the cited comparison

proof.text: Let $e_m:D\otimes_B A_m\to A_m$ be the reduction of $e$. For local homogeneous generators the two composites with reduction send $(b\otimes x)\otimes(b'\otimes f)$ to the class of $(-1)^{\deg x\deg f}bb'f(x)$. Hence the quotient squares commute strictly, and the $e_m$ are a morphism of strict towers. On both products it commutes with $1-s$, so the induced cone map $\widehat e=R\varprojlim_m e_m$ satisfies $\widehat e\,\chi_D=\chi_B e$: the product components agree by those quotient squares and both shifted-product components of the units are zero. The completed evaluation is $\widehat{\operatorname{ev}}=\chi_B^{-1}\widehat e$, by the completed tensor/internal-Hom adjunction (completion of ordinary evaluation into a complete target). Consequently $\widehat{\operatorname{ev}}\,\chi_D=e$ as derived morphisms; this is equality of the specified cone maps before localization.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.11: completed evaluation; strict quotient/cone computation

proof.text: The perfect models have finite Tor amplitude: their tensors with a degree-zero module have terms only in their fixed finite degree intervals. Thus the point-tensor theorem applies to $C,J$. On these models its canonical comparison $\tau$ is the inverse of $\Gamma(s,\chi_D)\beta$: balancing gives the ordinary sections tensor map, and the integral coefficient construction then applies the quotient-tower completion map. This description uses the same quotient maps in step 6 and hence the same zero shifted-product component; the inverse on an ordinary pure tensor is induced by $1\otimes x$ and $h$, so no alternate tensor or completion isomorphism is being substituted. Applying sections to step 7 and precomposing with $\beta$ now yields $\Gamma(s,\widehat{\operatorname{ev}})\Gamma(s,\chi_D)\beta=\Gamma(s,e)\beta=\operatorname{ev}_{P,R}(1\otimes q_P)$. Substitute $\Gamma(s,\chi_D)\beta=\tau^{-1}$ and compose with $\tau$. This is exactly the displayed equality of the statement in $D(R)$.
